subtitle: Lesson 29 · Capstone: Running a Real Application on Kubernetes

code:
FROM node:20-slim AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY src ./src

FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20-debian12 AS runtime
ARG ENTRYPOINT_FILE
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app /app
USER nonroot
ENTRYPOINT ["node"]
CMD ["/app/src/placeholder.js"]
caption: A build arg selects api.js or worker.js at build time -- one multi-stage Dockerfile, two images.

code:
docker build --build-arg ENTRYPOINT_FILE=src/api.js \
  -t registry.harrowcreek.dev/order-api:1.0.0 .
docker build --build-arg ENTRYPOINT_FILE=src/worker.js \
  -t registry.harrowcreek.dev/order-worker:1.0.0 .

docker push registry.harrowcreek.dev/order-api:1.0.0
docker push registry.harrowcreek.dev/order-worker:1.0.0
caption: A real version tag, not latest -- the only way a rollback has something to roll back to.

steps.label: order-api Deployment + Service
steps.sub: 3 replicas, port 8080, exposed via a ClusterIP Service

steps.label: order-worker Deployment only
steps.sub: 2 replicas, no ports, no Service -- it only drains a queue

steps.label: kubectl apply -f
steps.sub: Both objects created from plain YAML, no Helm yet

code:
kubectl apply -f api-deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f worker-deployment.yaml

kubectl get pods -l app=order-api
kubectl get svc order-api
kubectl get endpoints order-api
caption: Running isn't enough -- READY 1/1 on every pod, and real endpoints behind the Service, is the proof.
